title: Slab compaction, hotset heuristics, and prefetch coordinator for paged-KV to reduce decode stalls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: For large-sequence workloads served with paged attention, decode-time stalls spike when KV pages are fragmented across slabs or when the hot working set migrates between GPUs. Current page allocation is single-pass and eviction is LRU-ish, which increases head-of-line latency for tail requests and prevents reuse of compacted tiles. This ticket implements an integrated approach: a slab-aware compaction/defragmentation background worker, an adaptive hotset retention heuristic that biases allocation and retention toward frequently reused pages, and a prefetch coordinator that schedules prefill→decode handoffs to avoid blocking the decode pipeline. Additionally, expose a small kernel-selection hook so the runtime can pick a compact-optimized kernel path for pages that are tightly packed (improves throughput for quantized kernels).
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile decode latency for mixed short/long sessions improves by >=15% on benchmark workload (mix A) compared to baseline
Tail stall events (decode stalls waiting on KV fetch) reduced by >=50% on synthetic spike tests
Background compaction runs do not increase average token cost by more than 2% (measured in GPU utilization and token/sec)
Prefetch coordinator correctly sequences prefill and decode such that prefill misses <5% for top-10 hotset pages
New kernel-selection hook is exercised in at least two runtime unit tests and one end-to-end perf test
Feature guarded behind runtime flag and rollout toggle, observability (metrics/tracing) added for compaction runs, prefetch hits/misses, and kernel-path taken
implementation_plan: Design: define slab metadata layout (per-slab usage bitmap, fragment list) and compaction invariants (atomic move semantics)
Hotset heuristic: implement frequency+recency score (decayed counters) used to bias eviction and pin hot slabs for a configurable retention window
Prefetch coordinator: scheduler that maps prefill requests to decode lanes, allowing blocking prefetch for the next-k tokens and soft prefetch for lower priority pages
Compactor: background worker that performs in-place compaction when GPU utilization < threshold or on memory pressure, with safe migration to new slab slots and update of page pointers
Kernel hook: add lightweight API for slab-density hint passed to kernel selector so quantized/packed kernels can be chosen for dense slabs
Integration: add runtime flag 'kv_slab_compaction_v1' and per-customer rollout control in console
Tests: microbenchmarks for compaction throughput, integration tests for decode latency, fault injection tests for mid-compaction crashes
Docs: update runtime operator docs with config knobs and troubleshooting guidance
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime flag + canary rollout to 5% of traffic on dedicated pools
Observe critical metrics for 48h: decode latency p50/p95/p99, prefetch hit-rate, compaction failure rate
If stable, increase to 25% for another 48h, then full roll to dedicated clusters over 1 week
For hosted API, enable only on regions with spare capacity and enabled telemetry; do not enable for private clusters unless explicitly requested
Provide automatic rollback trigger if tail latency regresses by >10% or compaction error rate >0.1%
comments: 2025-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial design doc uploaded. Observed 120ms tail stalls on mix-A with current allocator; need hot retention to avoid repetitive page thrash.

2025-02-25 - Marco Nguyen: Implemented compaction prototype. Verified correctness under unit tests; noticed compactor causes micro-spikes when migrating >8 pages in a single batch. Plan to rate-limit migration and add backpressure to the scheduler.
2025-02-28 - Sophie Lee (SRE): Suggested compaction only run when GPU queue depth < 40% to avoid contention with active decodes. Added as config knob.

2025-03-02 - Marco Nguyen: Prefetch coordinator prototype schedules prefill slightly late for some long-sequence streams. Hypothesis: decode lanes starve when prefetch uses same CPU worker; moving prefetch to dedicated IO thread improved hit-rate by 12% in local tests.
2025-03-04 - Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to add kernel hook test and to tighten prefetch miss SLA. Scheduling follow-up call with compiler team to discuss kernel-density hints.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation and improves hotset locality but can introduce transient latency spikes; to mitigate we limit compaction concurrency and prefer low-util windows. Hotset heuristics introduce state that increases memory for counters (~1-2% memory overhead) but yields large tail latency improvements for bursty traffic. Kernel-selection hint is intentionally minimal (enum: DENSE|SPARSE|UNKNOWN) to avoid frequent recompilation or complex ABI changes.
